explanation: A 10-pack of Wrigley's Juicy Fruit gum was scanned at a Marsh supermarket in Troy, Ohio, on 26 June 1974. Its stripes were the Universal Product Code, which US grocers had agreed on in 1973.

claims.text: On 26 June 1974, a pack of Wrigley's Juicy Fruit chewing gum became the first product sold with a barcode (UPC) scan at a supermarket checkout.
The first barcode-scanned product was not cornflakes, teabags or toothpaste.
The pack scanned was a 10-pack of Juicy Fruit, at a Marsh supermarket in Troy, Ohio.
The US grocery industry agreed on the Universal Product Code in 1973.
